file_name: New Titanic Jacaranda General Spares v Omil & another (Commercial Case E095of2026) 2026SCC235(KLR) (31August2026) (Ruling)
parties: New Titanic Jacaranda General Spares v Omil & another
_note: Employer alleged employee stole cash. Struck out for want of jurisdiction: SCC Act s.13(5) excludes employment/labour relations claims. Respondents win on preliminary objection.

Road traffic/insurance matter. Respondent applied to set aside default judgment, claiming non-service and insurer (Corporate Insurance, under statutory management) should have defended. Application dismissed; original judgment and consequential orders stand.

Contract of bailment. 49,000 gunny bags stolen from appellant's warehouse. Court held employer liable for fraud/theft by servants. Appeal against refusal to set aside ex-parte judgment dismissed. Manju Patel (Respondent in appeal) wins.

file_name_on_disk: Nonny Gathoni Njenga  another v Catherine Masitsa  another 2014KEHC6468(KLR).pdf
file_name: Nonny Gathoni Njenga & another v Catherine Masitsa & another 2014KEHC6468(KLR)
parties: Nonny Gathoni Njenga & another v Catherine Masitsa & another
_note: Copyright contempt ruling. Plaintiffs alleged KTN (Standard Group) broadcast their 'WEDDINGS WITH NONI GATHONI' show in breach of injunction. Ruling on admissibility of DVD evidence: DVDs inadmissible without Evidence Act s.106B(4) certificate; court allowed Plaintiffs to remedy this. Procedural ruling only — no final winner. Costs in the cause.

Evidence Act s.106B ruling. Plaintiff's application to produce WhatsApp/SMS electronic records dismissed — no certificate of electronic record produced. Underlying civil dispute topic not determinable from this procedural ruling.

Defamation/libel appeal. Appellant sued Respondent for libel via WhatsApp group messages. Trial magistrate dismissed for lack of admissible evidence (no Evidence Act s.106B certificate for WhatsApp screenshots). High Court upheld dismissal; appeal dismissed for lack of merit. NOT an appeal from an SCC — original suit was before Hon. E. Obina (Senior Principal Magistrate), Kisumu Civil No. E056 of 2022.

Respondents (Standard Group & journalist) prevail on 3 of 4 challenged items. Underlying suit is defamation (funeral home operator v media company).
Criminal case. Ruling on admissibility of CCTV footage CD as electronic evidence (Evidence Act s.106B). CD ruled inadmissible without the required certificate. Kept excluded per instruction.

file_name: Safaricom Limited v Ocean View Beach Hotel Limited & 2 others 2010KECA346(KLR)
parties: Safaricom Limited v Ocean View Beach Hotel Limited & 2 others
_note: Commercial dispute (arbitration clause). Safaricom sought stay of High Court order (Koome J, HCCC 394 of 2009) pending appeal. Court struck out Koome J's ruling and granted 28-day interim protection over telecommunications equipment to allow parties to institute arbitral proceedings. Safaricom gets partial relief; matter directed to arbitration.
